top_choice_rationale: Buchwald and Hartwig made palladium-catalysed C-N coupling general by solving a distinct mechanistic problem (amido-palladium reductive elimination, catalyst inhibition by amines) through ligand design. The method is about thirty years mature, independently validated, routine in medicinal and process chemistry, and attributed cleanly to two groups, with Kosugi and Migita acknowledged as precursors by the 'general catalytic' wording. P001 is second: a real new principle, but with contested attribution across strands and no approved degrader yet. P003 is third: reversible-terminator chemistry is real molecule-making, but credit is entangled (Rothberg, Mayer, Ju) and it is partly platform engineering. No award is last.
